skill.description: Run a hosted Apify Actor to search public Google Maps businesses across geographic grids and return structured listings for market research.
skill.summary: Configure geographic business searches and retrieve JSON results through Apify.
skill.author: bolvein-firex

security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings are false positives involving documented Apify access, explicit input reads, Markdown formatting, or geographic terminology. No evidence found of prompt injection, covert exfiltration, shell injection, or attacker-controlled traversal in the supplied files. Hosted Actor internals were not supplied; execution sends search inputs to Apify and can incur disclosed account charges.

content.user_title: Map Local Business Coverage with Geographic Grid Searches
content.value_statement: Single Google Maps searches can miss businesses across larger areas. This skill configures grid searches through an Apify Actor and retrieves structured listings for market research.
actual_capabilities: Submit business queries with named locations, bounding boxes, circular areas, or GeoJSON polygon boundaries to the hosted Actor.
Configure grid zoom, per-cell limits, page depth, and total result limits through documented Actor inputs.
Request deduplication, minimum ratings, language selection, and optional place detail enrichment.
Run synchronous searches with a Node 18+ wrapper using APIFY_TOKEN and a JSON file or inline JSON input.
Follow documented curl examples to start asynchronous runs, inspect status, and retrieve dataset items.
Return JSON results with declared fields including business names, ratings, addresses, coordinates, phone numbers, and place identifiers.
limitations: Requires an Apify account and APIFY_TOKEN; hosted Actor usage can incur charges.
The supplied code is an API wrapper, not the hosted scraping implementation; listing completeness and field availability are not guaranteed.
Synchronous requests have a documented 300-second wait; asynchronous runs require completion checks before final dataset retrieval.
The wrapper prints JSON only; CSV conversion and market saturation metrics require separate processing.

use_cases.description: Repeat public business searches with recorded settings and retrieve datasets for separate client reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Location Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Find coffee shops within 2 km of Denver, Colorado, using a maximum of 50 results. Confirm current Apify pricing before running.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: test a small named-location search.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Competitor Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a search for HVAC businesses within 5 km of Austin, Texas. Enable deduplication and cap results at 200. Wait for approval before running.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: define a controlled competitor research dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Bounded Regional Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a pharmacy search with north 40.77, south 40.73, east -73.97, and west -74.01. Use zoom 15, deduplication, and a 500-result cap.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: configure an exact geographic bounding box.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Asynchronous Polygon Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my supplied GeoJSON polygon to prepare a restaurant search with enrichment, deduplication, and a 2,000-result cap. Confirm costs before starting asynchronously. Poll until completion before retrieving results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: manage a larger hosted run with explicit completion checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a small coffee shop search around Denver without running it.
output: Prepared search: coffee shops near Denver, Colorado, within a 2 km radius.
Limits: 20 places per cell and 50 total results, matching the bundled example.
Execution status: not started; confirm pricing and provide APIFY_TOKEN through the environment before running.

output_examples.input: Describe the expected business listing fields before I approve a scan.
output: Declared listing fields include business name, category, rating, review count, address, phone, website, coordinates, and place identifiers.
Optional enrichment requests additional details such as opening hours, price level, and closure status.
This is a field preview, not a live search result; availability depends on the hosted Actor and source listings.

best_practices: Start with a small boundary and a 50-result cap; inspect returned rows before increasing coverage or enrichment.
Confirm current Actor pricing and authorized data use; keep APIFY_TOKEN in the environment rather than prompts or shared reports.
Record boundaries and search settings; retain deduplication and verify asynchronous completion before comparing datasets.
anti_patterns: Treating collected listings as an exhaustive census or a calculated market saturation score.
Submitting cookies, session credentials, private account data, or unrelated local JSON files as search input.
Starting broad, enriched scans without checking costs, site terms, applicable laws, and result limits.

faq.question: Do I need an Apify account?
faq.answer: Yes. Set APIFY_TOKEN for authentication and check the Actor's current pricing before running searches.

faq.question: Does this skill scrape Google Maps locally?
faq.answer: No. The local wrapper submits search settings to a hosted Apify Actor and prints the returned dataset items.

faq.question: Which geographic boundaries can I use?
faq.answer: Documented inputs support named locations with a radius, bounding boxes, circle centers with a radius, and custom GeoJSON polygons.

faq.question: Will a grid search return every business?
faq.answer: Completeness is not guaranteed. Source rankings, geographic coverage, query choices, and configured limits affect the returned listings.

faq.question: Can I export CSV files directly?
faq.answer: The supplied wrapper prints JSON. Use separate conversion tooling or an available Apify dataset export option for CSV.

faq.question: How should I handle larger searches?
faq.answer: Use the documented asynchronous API flow. Check run status repeatedly until completion before retrieving the final dataset.
